title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Longue Marche notes, c. 1981). K is a field of finite type over Q, U is a smooth K-variety with function field L, and X is a smooth compactification whose boundary D = X \ U is a normal crossings divisor with components D_i, i in I (finite). For J ⊂ I, D_J = ∩_{j∈J} D_j is regular of codimension |J| (possibly empty). E_U denotes the arithmetic fundamental group, an extension of Gal(K̄/K) by the geometric group π_{U/K}.

Step 1. Calling J a simplex when D_J ≠ ∅ gives an abstract simplicial complex on I. This is the nerve of the covering of D by its components, i.e. the modern 'dual (intersection) complex' or 'boundary complex' of the compactification. Grothendieck asks what it means topologically.
- Its connected components correspond to those of D.
- They also correspond to those of U_∞ = X̂ \ D, where X̂ is the completion (formal or étale tubular neighbourhood) of X along D. U_∞ is the 'neighbourhood of infinity' of U.
- He notes this is a condition invariant with respect to the chosen compactification X of U.
- He remarks that if all non-empty D_J were ∞-connected (false in general: for maximal J, D_J can be a point, fine; but generally the strata are not contractible), the simplicial complex would give 'the homotopy type of U_∞'.

Step 2. He turns to the local situation along a stratum. X_J is an étale localisation (henselisation or tubular neighbourhood) of X along D_J, and U_J = X_J \ D_J is the trace of U. He states an exact sequence
(17) T^J → E^{L̄}_{U_J} → E_{D_J} → 1,
with T^J ≅ Ẑ(1)^J the tame inertia, i.e. the local monodromy around the |J| branches. This is the étale analogue of the fibration of the punctured polydisc bundle U_J → D_J with fibre (S^1)^J ≃ G_m^J. Base points are made explicit via a universal cover D̃_J, an induced universal pro-cover of X_J, covers Ũ_J → U, and the field L̃_J embedded in L̄.

Step 3 (next page). Comparing the homotopy exact sequences of U_J → X_J (≃ D_J) and U → Spec K, he finds that the composite π_2(D_J) → T^J → π_{U/K} vanishes, since π_2(Spec K) = 0. Hence, if T^J → π_{U/K} is injective (as in anabelian situations), the boundary map π_2(D_J) → T^J is zero. Topologically this boundary map is given by pairing spherical classes with the first Chern classes of the normal bundles N_{D_j}|D_J. The purpose is to understand the inertia subgroups attached to boundary strata, and their conjugacy classes, intrinsically inside Π_{L/K}.
errors: The heuristic that, with ∞-connected strata, the nerve would express the homotopy type of U_∞ is off. The nerve theorem gives the homotopy type of D (equivalently of the tubular neighbourhood X̂), not of the punctured neighbourhood U_∞. For a curve, the nerve is discrete while U_∞ is a disjoint union of circles. U_∞ is rather a torus-bundle-like object over D.
In (17), the left map T^J → E_{U_J} need not be injective. Its kernel is the image of π_2(D_J) under the normal-bundle Chern class pairing; Grothendieck himself worries about this on the next page.

The hypothesis 'T^J → π_{U/K} injective' fails in general. Example: U = A^2 ⊂ P^2 with D a line: π_1 is trivial and π_2(P^1) → Ẑ(1) is surjective via c_1(O(1)). So the conclusion is only conditional, valid for 'anabelian' U, e.g. hyperbolic curves or iterated fibrations of them.

ideas.what: Simplicial complex on the index set of boundary components, simplices = non-empty intersections D_J
ideas.modern_name: dual complex / boundary complex of an snc compactification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Danilov (1975); homotopy invariance Thuillier (2007), Stepanov; de Fernex–Kollár–Xu (2017); Payne

ideas.what: Neighbourhood at infinity U_∞ = X̂ \ D and the independence of its invariants from the compactification
ideas.modern_name: homotopy type at infinity / punctured tubular neighbourhood; boundary of Borel–Serre-like compactification
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; étale version: Fujiwara, Harbater, Cox

ideas.what: Exact sequence T^J → π_1(U_J) → π_1(D_J) → 1 for the localisation along a normal crossings stratum
ideas.modern_name: tame fundamental group along an NCD; log fundamental group of a log point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck–Murre (1971); SGA1 XIII; Abhyankar's lemma; Kato–Illusie log étale

ideas.what: Comparison of the homotopy sequences, giving vanishing of π_2(D_J) → T^J (normal-bundle Chern classes on spheres) when inertia injects into the geometric fundamental group
ideas.modern_name: injectivity of inertia / cuspidal decomposition groups in anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mochizuki, Hoshi–Mochizuki (decomposition/inertia groups of log configuration spaces)

missed.claim: In the anabelian programme Grothendieck already asks for the topological meaning of the dual complex of the boundary and its relation to the 'neighbourhood at infinity' U_∞. He also stresses invariance with respect to the chosen compactification. This anticipates the later study of the homotopy type of boundary complexes (Thuillier, de Fernex–Kollár–Xu) and links it to Galois-theoretic data (inertia classes in π_{U/K}).
missed.quote: on trouve, sur I une structure de ensemble simplicial – quelle est sa signification topologique ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Links boundary/dual complexes (Berkovich skeleta) with anabelian reconstruction of the configuration of inertia subgroups; this combination is little explored.

missed.claim: Conditional observation: for anabelian U (inertia T^J injecting into π_{U/K}), the profinite boundary map π_2(D_J) → T^J, i.e. the Chern classes of the normal bundles of the D_j restricted to D_J, must vanish on (profinite) spherical classes. This is a constraint on compactifications of anabelian varieties that he does not pursue.
missed.quote: on conclurait que π_2(D_J) → T^J est nul !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives a testable geometric constraint relating anabelianity to the normal bundle geometry of boundary strata.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly a heuristic set-up of known local structure (tame π_1 along an NCD). The early question about the topological meaning and invariance of the dual complex, and the π_2/normal-bundle constraint for anabelian varieties, are modestly interesting but tentative.
transcription_corrections: 'une condition imposée p.r. à la "complexification" choisie X de U' should read 'une condition invariante p.r. à la "compactification" choisie X de U'.
'les comp. connexes[?] connexes correspondent' is likely 'les comp. connexes (de I) correspondent aux comp. connexes de D'.
'le {+localisé[?]+} complété de X' is probably 'le complété formel de X le long de D' (the insertion is uncertain).
'si J[?] fini[?] D_J réduit : un point !' is likely 'si J maximal, D_J [pouvant être] réduit à un point !' (uncertain).
'Considérons E_{U_J} (de façon précise, E^{L̄}_U, si on localise p.r. à ...)': the superscript is probably L̄_J / L̃_J, referring to the choice of base point.
